analysis.investment_thesis: CP Plus is India's leading surveillance brand operating in a secular security-tech tailwind, but at ₹26,673 Cr market cap and 105x trailing P/E, it is priced for perfection many years out — a cardinal sin against the SMILE framework. The 2025 net profit of ₹351 Cr is heavily inflated by ₹259 Cr of "Other Income" (likely listing/divestment gains), making the underlying earnings quality far weaker than headline numbers suggest.
key_strengths: Brand leadership: CP Plus is India's #1 surveillance brand with 20.2% revenue CAGR (2020-25) reaching ₹3,112 Cr
Promoter conviction: 76.91% promoter holding — strong skin in the game
Debt virtually eliminated: Borrowings collapsed from ₹436 Cr (FY24) to ₹128 Cr (FY25), D/E at 0.08
key_risks: Stratospheric valuation: 105x P/E and 68.8x EV/EBITDA — zero margin of safety for any growth disappointment
Earnings quality red flag: ₹259 Cr Other Income in FY25 drove net profit jump; strip it out and adjusted PAT is ~₹150-160 Cr, implying real P/E closer to 170x
Cash flow illusion: FCF was only ₹1 Cr in FY25 despite ₹351 Cr reported PAT — operating CF of just ₹27 Cr signals working capital strain
red_flags: Market cap ₹26,673 Cr — 26x outside Kedia's 100-1000 Cr sweet spot
P/E 105x vs Kedia target of 8-15x; forward P/E of 61.7x still deeply expensive
Other Income spiked to ₹259 Cr in FY25 (vs -₹12 Cr in FY24) — one-time boost masking the real earnings base
Equity reserves jumped ₹1,153 Cr in FY25 suggesting large capital raise that diluted per-share value
Operating margins remain modest at 11.2% despite scale — limited pricing power against Chinese hardware competition
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CP Plus is a genuinely strong franchise — India's dominant surveillance brand with a 30-year track record, a wide distribution moat, and a smart pivot toward AI/IoT services (OnVigil, cloud storage). Revenue CAGR of 20.2% and EBITDA CAGR of 33% over five years show real operating leverage. Promoter holding at 76.9% is exemplary. The business ticks the E (extra-large market) and L (large aspiration with AI surveillance) boxes of SMILE. But CP Plus is no longer a hidden gem — it's a fully discovered, institutionally owned large-cap at ₹26,673 Cr.

The numbers fall apart under scrutiny. The FY25 PAT of ₹351 Cr is propped up by ₹259 Cr of Other Income — strip that away and core earnings are ₹150-160 Cr, putting real trailing P/E near 170x. Free cash flow was ₹1 Cr on ₹3,112 Cr revenue, and OCF was negative in FY24 (-₹180 Cr). The equity base nearly quadrupled in FY25 (₹424 Cr → ₹1,587 Cr), suggesting a large equity raise that flatters the balance sheet but dilutes returns. For Vijay Kedia, who needs an 8-15x P/E entry with room for a 10x re-rating, this stock offers no viable entry point today.
